title: Options, timeouts and [GeneratedRegex]
summary: RegexOptions that matter in production (CultureInvariant, NonBacktracking, IgnorePatternWhitespace), match timeouts and RegexMatchTimeoutException, and source-generated regexes as the default for fixed patterns.

steps.title: The options that matter
body: `RegexOptions` are flags you combine with `|`. These are the ones you will meet in real code:
| Option | Effect | Inline |
| `IgnoreCase` | case-insensitive | `(?i)` |
| `CultureInvariant` | with IgnoreCase: case rules that do not depend on the machine's culture | |
| `Multiline` | `^` and `$` match at every line | `(?m)` |
| `Singleline` | `.` also matches `\n` | `(?s)` |
| `ExplicitCapture` | only named groups capture; `(...)` just groups | `(?n)` |
| `IgnorePatternWhitespace` | spaces in the pattern are ignored and `#` starts a comment | `(?x)` |
| `Compiled` | generate IL at run time: slower start, faster matching | |
| `NonBacktracking` (.NET 7+) | linear time, whatever the input; no lookarounds, backreferences or atomic groups | |
| `ECMAScript` | JavaScript-like behaviour, e.g. `\d` is only `0-9` | |
Two worth arguing for in review:
- **`IgnoreCase | CultureInvariant`** for identifiers, keywords and protocol text, so the result is the same on
every server.
- **`NonBacktracking`** when the pattern or the input is untrusted: no input can make it run for minutes.

steps.prompt: Match each option to what it changes.
pairs: `^` and `$` match at the start and end of every line
spaces are ignored and `#` starts a comment

steps.prompt: A gateway checks `Regex.IsMatch(role, "^admin$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase)`. It works everywhere except on one server, whose culture is `tr-TR`, where the role `ADMIN` is rejected. Why, and what is the fix?
options: In Turkish, `I` lower-cases to dotless `ı` and `i` upper-cases to dotted `İ`, so `I` and `i` are not a case pair. Add `RegexOptions.CultureInvariant`.
`IgnoreCase` only works for ASCII letters, so use `[Aa][Dd][Mm][Ii][Nn]`.
`^` and `$` behave differently in some cultures; use `\A` and `\z`.
steps.explain: This is the "Turkish i" problem. With `IgnoreCase` .NET uses the current culture's case rules, and Turkish and Azerbaijani pair the letters differently. `CultureInvariant` makes the check identical on every machine. The same bug hits `ToUpper()`, which is why code uses `ToUpperInvariant()` and `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase`.

steps.title: A pattern with comments
prompt: Config files hold durations like `1h30m`, `45s` or `2h`: hours, minutes and seconds, each optional, in that
order, at least one present. Write a pattern with named groups `h`, `m` and `s` (ASCII digits).
The **x** flag (IgnorePatternWhitespace) is on and fixed, so you can space the parts out. End the pattern with a
`# comment` saying what it does (a check requires one). The next person to read it will thank you.
hints: Each part is an optional group like `(?:(?<h>[0-9]+)h)?`. With all three optional, the empty string would match: start with a lookahead `(?=[0-9])`.
steps.explain: In C# you would write the pattern over several lines in a verbatim string, one part per line with its own comment, and pass `RegexOptions.IgnorePatternWhitespace`. A real space then has to be written as `\ ` or `[ ]`.

steps.title: Timeouts: a safety net
body: Some patterns backtrack exponentially on unlucky input (module 2). If the pattern or the input comes from
outside, one request can then keep a thread busy for minutes: that is a denial of service (ReDoS). By default
.NET regexes have **no timeout** (`Regex.InfiniteMatchTimeout`).
```csharp fragment
var regex = new Regex(pattern, RegexOptions.CultureInvariant, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250));
try
accepted = regex.IsMatch(input);
catch (RegexMatchTimeoutException e)
logger.LogWarning("Regex timed out after {Timeout} on {Length} chars", e.MatchTimeout, e.Input.Length);
accepted = false;   // treat as invalid: do not crash the request
To protect every regex in the process, including those inside libraries, set a default **at startup, before
any regex is created**:
```csharp
AppContext.SetData("REGEX_DEFAULT_MATCH_TIMEOUT", TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1));
A timeout limits the damage; it does not fix the pattern. For untrusted patterns, `NonBacktracking` removes
the problem. Log the input's length, not the input: it may hold personal data.

steps.prompt: A regex is built with `TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250)`, and an input arrives that would take the engine minutes. What does `regex.IsMatch(input)` do?
options: Returns `false` at once, because the engine detects the bad pattern
Keeps running: the timeout applies only to `Matches`
steps.explain: A timeout never turns into a silent `false`: the call throws, every method of the instance honours it, and the exception carries `Input`, `Pattern` and `MatchTimeout`. Your code decides what a timeout means, usually "reject", and logs it so you find the pattern.

steps.title: [GeneratedRegex]: the default for fixed patterns
body: Since .NET 7, a **source generator** can turn a constant pattern into plain C# while your project builds:
```csharp
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
static partial class Patterns
// .NET 7+: a partial method
[GeneratedRegex(@"\b[A-Z]{2,5}-[0-9]+\b", RegexOptions.CultureInvariant, matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 250)]
public static partial Regex TicketKey();
// .NET 9+ (C# 13): a partial property
[GeneratedRegex(@"[0-9]+")]
public static partial Regex Digits { get; }
// Patterns.TicketKey().IsMatch(s)    Patterns.Digits.Count(s)
Why it is the default for any pattern you know at compile time:
- **No startup cost**: nothing is parsed or compiled at run time, unlike `RegexOptions.Compiled`.
- **Native AOT and trimming friendly**: no IL is emitted at run time.
- **Readable**: the generated matcher is C# you can open and step through, with comments explaining it.
- **One cached instance**, created on first use and shared by all threads.
The class must be `partial`. Analyzer **SYSLIB1045** flags `new Regex("constant")` and offers to convert it.
Keep `new Regex(...)` for patterns that only exist at run time.

steps.prompt: Arrange the lines into a source-generated regex.
steps.explain: The attribute sits on a `static partial` method returning `Regex`, inside a `partial` class. The generator writes the method's body.

items: The ticket key format, the same in every build
A pattern a user types into a log search box
Per-tenant validation rules loaded from the database
SKU validation in a Native AOT microservice
The log-line parser called on every request
A pattern built at startup from a list of banned words in config
steps.explain: If the pattern is a constant in your source, generate it. If it only exists at run time, build it with `new Regex` (with a timeout or `NonBacktracking`, since it came from outside), and cache it if it is reused.

steps.title: Symptom: the saved search stopped working
prompt: **Symptom.** The log viewer now runs every saved search with `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking`, so a hostile
pattern cannot hang it. One saved search fails with:
```text
System.NotSupportedException: Regular expression construct (?<=...) is not supported with RegexOptions.NonBacktracking
Rewrite it without lookarounds: match `user=` followed by the user name, and capture the name in group 1.
`superuser=` must not count.
hints: Match the prefix instead of looking behind for it, and capture what follows: `user=(\w+)`.
Add `\b` in front so `superuser=` does not match: `\buser=(\w+)`.
steps.explain: NonBacktracking supports groups and captures, but not lookarounds, backreferences, atomic groups or conditionals. The fix is common: consume the context and capture the part you want, then read group 1 instead of the whole match.

steps.title: Generate the ticket key regex
prompt: Write `static partial class Patterns` with a source-generated `public static partial Regex TicketKey()` for
keys like `OPS-311`: a word boundary, 2 to 5 capital letters, a dash, ASCII digits, a word boundary.
Give it `RegexOptions.CultureInvariant` and a 250 ms timeout (`matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 250`).
The tests call `Patterns.TicketKey()`. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
Dojo.Eq("OPS-311 is a key", true, Patterns.TicketKey().IsMatch("OPS-311"));
Dojo.Eq("finds the key inside a sentence", "PAY-7", Patterns.TicketKey().Match("fixes PAY-7 today").Value);
Dojo.Eq("lower case is not a key", false, Patterns.TicketKey().IsMatch("ops-311"));
Dojo.Eq("six letters is not a key", false, Patterns.TicketKey().IsMatch("TOOLONG-1"));
Dojo.Eq("one cached instance", true, ReferenceEquals(Patterns.TicketKey(), Patterns.TicketKey()));
Dojo.Eq("a 250 ms timeout", TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250), Patterns.TicketKey().MatchTimeout);
{{CODE}}

steps.title: ParseDuration, the production version
prompt: Write `static partial class Durations` with `public static TimeSpan? Parse(string text)` for durations like
`1h30m`, `45s`, `90m` or `1h30m15s`. Return `null` for anything else.
- Use a source-generated regex with named groups `h`, `m`, `s` and ASCII digits `[0-9]`, anchored with `^`
and `\z` (`$` would also accept a trailing newline).
- The text comes from user config, so give the regex `matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 250`, and catch
`RegexMatchTimeoutException`: a timeout means "not a valid duration", not a crash.
- `new TimeSpan(hours, minutes, seconds)` builds the result; `90m` is 1:30:00.
`System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
Dojo.Eq("1h30m", (TimeSpan?)new TimeSpan(1, 30, 0), Durations.Parse("1h30m"));
Dojo.Eq("45s", (TimeSpan?)new TimeSpan(0, 0, 45), Durations.Parse("45s"));
Dojo.Eq("2h", (TimeSpan?)new TimeSpan(2, 0, 0), Durations.Parse("2h"));
Dojo.Eq("90m is an hour and a half", (TimeSpan?)new TimeSpan(1, 30, 0), Durations.Parse("90m"));
Dojo.Eq("1h30m15s", (TimeSpan?)new TimeSpan(1, 30, 15), Durations.Parse("1h30m15s"));
Dojo.Check("an empty string is not a duration", Durations.Parse("") is null, "expected null");
Dojo.Check("30m1h is in the wrong order", Durations.Parse("30m1h") is null, "expected null");
Dojo.Check("1.5h is not supported", Durations.Parse("1.5h") is null, "expected null");
Dojo.Check("a trailing newline is rejected", Durations.Parse("2h\n") is null, "expected null: use \\z, not $");
Dojo.Try("Arabic-Indic digits are rejected, not a crash", () => Dojo.Check("\u0662h is not a duration", Durations.Parse("\u0662h") is null, "expected null: use [0-9], not \\d"));
{{CODE}}
hints: Declare `[GeneratedRegex(@"^(?=[0-9])(?:(?<h>[0-9]+)h)?...\z", RegexOptions.CultureInvariant, matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 250)] private static partial Regex Pattern();`
In `Parse`: match inside `try`, read each group with `m.Groups["h"].Success ? int.Parse(m.Groups["h"].Value) : 0`, and `catch (RegexMatchTimeoutException) { return null; }`.
